subject: Discovery recap: Private/VPC priorities, air-gap considerations, success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medteva.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T14:08:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's Private deployment call

Hi Elena — great to meet you and Luca on the call earlier. Thanks for walking us through MedTeva's constraints; below is a concise recap so we're aligned on priorities and next actions. 

High-level pain points you called out:
- Regulatory requirement: data residency in the EU and retained audit logs for 7 years.
- Network constraint: isolated VPC with egress controls; limited ability to open outbound ports from model-serving hosts.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (BYOK) via your AWS KMS account; HSM-backed keys are preferred for production.
- Air-gap possible for certain workloads: production model artifacts must be moved through an approved media-transfer process and hosts will live on a segregated LAN.

Current stack (as stated):
- Primary cloud: eu-west-1 (AWS), dedicated account per environment.
- Identity: Okta for SSO; internal automation uses a Bastion host + SSM exec.
- Logging: ELK stack managed by MedTeva; SIEM ingestion required for all inference logs.

Success criteria for Phase 1 (pilot):
1) Private control plane with no customer data leaving MedTeva's VPC unless explicitly routed (S3 egress paths locked).
2) KMS integration using your CMK with envelope encryption and auditability.
3) Demonstrated model deploy workflow that respects your air-gap process (artifact signing + offline transfer).
4) Latency: 95th percentile inference latency under 120ms for the sample traffic we discussed (batch size 1, seq len ~512).
5) Security: SOC2+ISO27001 equivalent controls and signed NDA + BAA in place.

Immediate next steps (what I will do):
- Share a short architecture sketch showing: control plane placement, data plane options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), and an air-gap artifact flow (attached). (Action: Marissa) — ETA: EOD tomorrow.
- Confirm Redwood's KMS integration model and an outline of the key-handover process we use for HSM-backed keys. (Action: Ben) — ETA: 48 hours.

Immediate next steps (what MedTeva will do):
- Share a sanitized network topology and firewall rules for the target account. (Action: Elena / IT) — ETA: 2 business days.
- Introduce procurement contact for a high-level SOW and licensing questions. (Action: Luca) — ETA: this week.

Attachments: medteva-network-sketch-v1.pdf (sketch from call), redwood-private-highlevel-arch.png (proposed patterns).

If that aligns, I'll open a mutual action plan in HubSpot and we can tentatively schedule a technical deep-dive with Ben for Tuesday next week. Thanks again — looking forward to progressing.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is very clear and matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from my side:

1) On the air-gap: our security team requires checksum verification and signed manifests for any model artifacts transferred into the isolated environment; can Redwood sign releases (GPG or equivalent) and provide a reproducible build hash?
2) For KMS: we will provide a CMK in our account. HSM backing is preferred but not mandatory for the pilot — what minimal access does Redwood need to perform envelope encryption without storing key material?
3) Logging: all inference request/response metadata (no PII) should be forwarded to our ELK endpoint over an approved syslog TLS tunnel; is Redwood able to push logs rather than MedTeva pulling them?

I'll attach a redacted network sketch and a short list of required compliance documents (NDA + SOC2 report). Luca, looping you for procurement timing — we want to line up budget and an SOW for Oct.

> Hi Elena — great to meet you and Luca on the call earlier...
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medteva.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:15:00Z
Subject: RE: Quick recap + next steps from today's Private deployment call — technical notes

Hi Elena — thanks for the follow-ups, answers inline below. High-level: we can meet your constraints with a Private deployment + optional air-gapped model promotion flow. Short answers: yes, yes, and yes, with details.

1) Artifact signing: Redwood can produce signed release bundles. We currently support SHA256 manifests signed with a company-managed GPG key; for higher assurance we can integrate an external signing key workflow (customer-supplied) during the release promotion step. We can also provide reproducible build instructions for your security team to verify.

2) KMS integration: for envelope encryption we require the ability to call Encrypt/Decrypt with your CMK for envelope keys. Redwood never stores raw CMK material. We will provide a minimal IAM role for the service to call kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt on the CMK and audit those calls. For HSM-backed keys, the flow is identical from an API perspective; the key origin is handled inside your KMS.

3) Logging: Redwood can stream structured inference telemetry to an HTTPS ingestion endpoint or to a syslog/TLS endpoint that you control. For the pilot we recommend HTTPS push to a MedTeva ingestion gateway so you retain control over transport and egress.

Network/egress options to consider:
- PrivateLink endpoint per region (preferred for cross-account control).
- VPC peering with strict routing tables and NAT restrictions.
- Fully isolated hosts with a one-way gateway for artifact ingestion during the air-gap process.

Risks & assumptions:
- We assume a small set of test models for pilot (1–2) to keep artifact transfer and signing small.
- We will need a service account for initial bootstrap with limited IAM.

Deliverables I'll prepare this week:
- KMS integration runbook (how to provision IAM role + audit log pattern)
- Artifact signing template and verification checklist
- Minimal deployment topology options (PrivateLink / Peering / Offline transfer)

I'll attach the runbook draft after internal review. If it helps, Vanessa can coordinate a joint call with your security team next Wednesday.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
